note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question b, wording: The right option is the only one with a hedged 'can'. Every distractor uses an absolute ('only', 'only', 'no effect'), so a student could pick the answer by spotting the qualifier without knowing the idea.
- Card, fact: 'Countries must cooperate by agreement' oversimplifies Mekong management. The 1995 Mekong Agreement (Mekong River Commission) covers only Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. China and Myanmar are only dialogue partners, and China builds upstream dams without a binding agreement. Better: 'countries need to cooperate, but not all have signed the same agreement'.

rejected.title: Comparing inland water in Australia and another country
card: The Murray-Darling Basin in Australia is shared by several states and territories. Its water is used for farms, towns, industry and the environment.
The Mekong River runs through six countries: China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. Millions of people rely on it for fishing, farming and water.
Both rivers face competing uses. Dams and water taken upstream can change how much water, and how much sediment, reaches the people and wildlife downstream.
The management differs. The Murray-Darling is managed within one country, under Australian laws. The Mekong crosses national borders, so countries must cooperate by agreement.
rejected.remember: Both rivers have competing uses. They differ in who must agree on how to manage them.

a.q: What is a main difference between managing the Mekong and the Murray-Darling?
opts: The Mekong crosses countries, so agreements are needed
The Mekong has no dams, so it needs no rules
The Murray-Darling is not used by farms or towns
The Murray-Darling is shared by several countries
a.why: The Mekong flows through several countries, so they must cooperate by agreement. The Murray-Darling is within Australia, so Australian laws apply. It is shared by states, not countries.

b.q: A new dam on the upper Mekong traps sediment, and fishers in Cambodia downstream catch fewer fish. What does this suggest about the Murray-Darling?
opts: Murray-Darling dams can also cut flows to users downstream
Murray-Darling dams have no effect, as it is in one country
Murray-Darling dams only affect users who live upstream
Murray-Darling dams cause harm only across state borders
b.why: Dams and water taken upstream can change the water and sediment that reach people downstream, on either river. Being within one country changes who manages the river, not the way water flows, so the Murray-Darling is not free of these effects.
b.clue: Does the way water flows depend on a border?

opts: The Mekong crosses borders, so countries need to cooperate
The Mekong has no dams, so countries need no shared rules
The Murray-Darling is not used by farms, towns or industry
The Murray-Darling is shared by several separate countries
